theory.category: Instructions used at the beginning of a session
theory.example: Introducing the aim of the lesson, the teacher says, “We'll learn how to describe our daily routines today.”

theory.category: Instructions used at the beginning of a session
theory.example: Before starting a new activity, the teacher asks, “Are you ready?”

theory.category: Instructions used at the beginning of a session
theory.example: The teacher says, “Open your books at page 42 and look at exercise three.”

theory.category: Instructions used at the beginning of a session
theory.example: To find the reading text, the teacher instructs, “Turn to page 18.”
After demonstrating the solution, the teacher asks, “Do you get it?”
While explaining the grammar rule, the teacher pauses: “Are you with me?”
Seeing a puzzled expression, the teacher asks, “Are you OK? Would you like another example?”

theory.ru: Вы понимаете, о чём я говорю?
theory.example: After a detailed explanation, the teacher checks, “Do you follow me?”
Halfway through the instructions, the teacher asks, “OK so far?”
When a late pupil knocks, the teacher says, “Come in.”
During a fire drill, the teacher instructs the class, “Go out calmly and follow me.”
Before a speaking activity, the teacher says, “Stand by your desks.”
To begin a short movement break, the teacher says, “Stand up.”
After the activity, the teacher says, “Sit down, please.”

theory.en: Come to the front of the class.
theory.ru: Выйдите к доске / к передней части класса.
theory.example: The teacher invites a volunteer: “Come to the front of the class and show us your drawing.”
After choosing a pupil to answer, the teacher says to the others, “Put your hands down.”

theory.ru: Поднимите учебники, чтобы их было видно.
theory.example: To check the covers, the teacher says, “Hold your books up so I can see them.”

theory.ru: Поднимите ручки, чтобы их было видно.
theory.example: Before a handwriting task, the teacher says, “Hold your pens up.”
During a reading lesson, the teacher says, “Open your books at page 75.”

theory.en: I want you all to join in.
theory.ru: Я хочу, чтобы все приняли участие.
theory.example: Before the discussion, the teacher says, “I want you all to join in.”
To invite a choral answer, the teacher says, “The whole class, please.”
Practising pronunciation, the teacher prompts, “All together now: three, two, one.”

theory.en: Come out and write it on the board.
theory.ru: Выйдите к доске и напишите это.
theory.example: The teacher asks a pupil, “Come out and write it on the board.”
Explaining the procedure, the teacher says, “First, read the question carefully.”
Before giving instructions, the teacher says, “First of all, listen to the dialogue.”
The teacher continues, “After that, compare your answers with a partner.”
Moving to the second step, the teacher says, “Then, write two examples.”
The teacher explains, “Next, discuss your ideas in pairs.”
After one pupil finishes reading, the teacher says, “Next one, please.”

theory.en: For the last thing today, let's ...
theory.example: Near the end of the class, the teacher says, “For the last thing today, let's review the new words.”

theory.en: Whose turn is it to read?
theory.example: Before reading aloud, the teacher asks, “Whose turn is it to read?”
When chatter interrupts the lesson, the teacher says, “Stop talking and listen, please.”
Pointing to a diagram on the board, the teacher says, “Look this way.”

theory.ru: Пока отложите это / Не трогайте это сейчас.
theory.example: When pupils start using materials too early, the teacher says, “Leave that alone now. We'll use it later.”
During a science demonstration, the teacher warns, “Be careful with the glass.”
While one pupil gives an answer, the teacher says, “Listen to what Anna is saying.”
After explaining the homework, the teacher asks, “Any questions?”
The teacher invites participation: “Who knows the answer?”
When a pupil speaks too quietly, the teacher says, “Louder, please!”
Encouraging a complete response, the teacher says, “A full sentence, please.”
After a correct answer, the teacher confirms, “Yes, that's right.”
The teacher listens to a pupil's explanation and responds, “Fine. Let's continue.”
When a pupil is close to the answer, the teacher says, “Almost. Try again.”
Looking at the next item in the text, the teacher asks, “What about this word?”
After hearing an unusual idea, the teacher responds, “That's interesting!”

theory.en: That really is very kind of you.
theory.ru: Это очень любезно с вашей стороны.
theory.example: When a pupil helps distribute materials, the teacher says, “That really is very kind of you.”
Reassuring a pupil who makes a small mistake, the teacher says, “Don't worry about it.”
Encouraging a hesitant pupil, the teacher says, “Have a go!”
After an incorrect attempt, the teacher says, “Have another try!”
After an excellent presentation, the teacher exclaims, “Magnificent!”
Checking an answer, the teacher confirms, “Right!”
After reviewing the work, the teacher says, “Fine! You can move on.”
The teacher praises a correct explanation: “Very good!”
After hearing an accurate answer, the teacher says, “That's very good.”
When the group finishes a difficult task, the teacher says, “Great stuff!”
The teacher tells the pupils after their performance, “Well done.”
After a successful group project, the teacher says, “You did a great job.”
When the pupil finds the correct word, the teacher says, “That's it!”
After a pupil explains the rule correctly, the teacher says, “Yes, you've got it.”
Reacting to a creative presentation, the teacher says, “Fantastic!”
After reading a pupil's short story, the teacher remarks, “That's nice.”

theory.ru: Это зависит от обстоятельств / от ситуации.
theory.example: When asked whether an expression is formal, the teacher replies, “It depends on the situation.”
After noticing better pronunciation, the teacher says, “You've improved a lot.”
Encouraging a nearly correct solution, the teacher says, “You're on the right lines.”
To reassure a pupil who is thinking, the teacher says, “There's no hurry. Take your time.”
After checking an incorrect answer, the teacher says, “Unfortunately not. Let's look at it again.”

theory.en: Good try, but not quite right.
theory.ru: Хорошая попытка, но ответ не совсем верный.
theory.example: The teacher gives supportive feedback: “Good try, but not quite right.”
On a pupil's special day, the teacher says, “Happy birthday!”
Before the winter holiday, the teacher wishes the class, “Merry Christmas!”
When a pupil arrives late, the teacher asks, “Did you oversleep?”
Noticing a pupil's late arrival, the teacher asks, “Did you miss your bus?”
After a pupil enters late, the teacher asks, “Where have you been?”

theory.ru: Постарайтесь, чтобы это больше не повторилось.
theory.example: After discussing repeated lateness, the teacher says, “Don't let it happen again.”
Before a competition, the teacher wishes the pupils, “Best of luck!”
When pupils win a school contest, the teacher says, “Congratulations!”

theory.ru: В следующий раз обязательно повезёт больше.
theory.example: After a disappointing result, the teacher encourages the group: “Better luck next time.”

theory.en: I hope you all have a good Christmas.
theory.ru: Надеюсь, вы все хорошо проведёте рождественские праздники.
theory.example: Before the holidays, the teacher says, “I hope you all have a good Christmas.”
Seeing a pupil return after an illness, the teacher asks, “Do you feel better today?”
After a pupil rests in the nurse's office, the teacher asks, “Are you better now?”

theory.en: I'll be back in a moment.
theory.example: Before stepping into the corridor, the teacher tells the class, “I'll be back in a moment.”

theory.en: I've got to go next door for a moment.
theory.ru: Мне нужно ненадолго выйти в соседний кабинет.
theory.example: The teacher tells a colleague, “I've got to go next door for a moment.”
Explaining why speaking is difficult, the teacher says, “I have a sore throat.”
After feeling unwell, the teacher says, “I have a headache.”

theory.en: Do you mind if I sit down?
theory.ru: Вы не возражаете, если я присяду?
theory.example: Feeling tired during a long activity, the teacher asks, “Do you mind if I sit down?”
